column2: In this vow taken, O god, if I die with it incomplete, may it be complete for me by your grace, Janardana.
A Brahmin giving up meat and the like, abandoning oil, should worship Hari; fasting on alternate days for three nights he shares Vishnu's world.
The Chandrayana-doer reaches Vishnu's world; the silent one is a vessel of liberation; the Prajapatya vower is a heaven-goer, living on barley meal and yavaka;
one living on milk and the like goes to heaven, as does one drinking pancha-gavya water; a man living on vegetables, roots and fruits goes to Vishnu's city;
avoiding meat, living on barley, avoiding juices, one goes to Hari. I shall tell the Kaumuda vow: having fasted in Ashvina,
on the twelfth one should worship Vishnu, anointing with lotuses, water lilies and the like; with ghee or sesame oil one should offer lamp and food;
Om homage to Vasudeva — one should worship with a jasmine garland. The Kaumuda vower obtains dharma, desire, wealth and liberation.
The month-long fasting vower, having worshipped Hari, obtains everything.
A night-eater on the eleventh in Chaitra should offer food; the vower of Vishnu's good vow goes to the golden abode of Vishnu at month's end;
eating pudding, giver of a pair of cows, the vower of the goddess becomes possessed of fortune; one who eats after offering to the ancestors and gods becomes a king.
The year-long vows are told; I tell the Sankranti vow. On the Sankranti, by night vigil a man becomes a dweller in heaven;
on the new-moon Sankranti by worshipping Shiva and the Sun; at the northern solstice by bathing Keshava with a prastha of ghee,
by a measure of thirty-two palas he is freed from all sins; having bathed him with ghee, milk and the rest he obtains the fruit at the equinoxes and the rest.
The Uma vow of women, giving prosperity, on the thirds and eighths: one should worship Gauri and Maheshvara too and obtain good fortune;
having worshipped Uma and Maheshvara one obtains non-separation and the rest. A woman keeping the Mula vow and the Umesha vow,
a woman devoted to the Sun, surely becomes a man.
In the west of the seat, "dham vam" — the forest-garland in the west; "sam ham lam cham tam yam" — Shrivatsa and Kaustubha in the water;
in the order of the ten limbs of Vishnu one should worship below "homage to Ananta"; the ten-limbed and Mahendra and the rest, and four pots in the east and so on;
arches, canopy, with the seeds of fire, wind and moon, the mandalas, having meditated in order, having saluted the body, he should then float;
then having meditated on one's own subtle form standing in the sky, immersed in white nectar, flowing from the moon's disc,
that very nectar, purified by the floating, is the seed of the self; one should imagine the self as a person being born:
I am born, myself Vishnu — one should place the twelve-fold seed: heart, head, crest, armor and weapon;
one should place again on chest, head, crest, back and eyes; having placed the weapon on the two hands, he becomes of divine body.
As in the self so in the god; likewise one should place on the disciple's body. Worship without remains is that worship of Hari in the heart;
with remains in the mandala and the like; the disciples, eyes bound, throw a flower; on whose image it falls, one should give that name.
Having seated the disciples at the left one should offer sesame, rice and ghee; having offered a hundred and eight, a thousand for purification of the body;
of the nine-fold formation, of the images and limbs, over a hundred; having given the full offering the teacher should initiate them, and be honored by them with wealth.
Atimukta likewise; Patala gives Vishnu's world; with oleander one reaches Vishnu's world, with hibiscus flowers one becomes meritorious;
with pavanti, kubjaka and the rest, and with tagara, one shares Vishnu's world; with karnikara Vishnu's world; with karunta, destruction of sin;
with lotuses, ketaki and kunda flowers the supreme goal; with vana flowers and black varvara one shares Hari's world;
with ashoka, tilaka, likewise those from atarusha, one shares liberation; with bilva leaves, with shami leaves the supreme goal;
with bhringaraja and tamala leaves one reaches Vishnu's world; Tulasi, called black and white, kalhara and water lilies;
lotus, red lotus, holy; Hari with a garland of a hundred lotuses; with nipa, arjuna, kadamba and fragrant vakula;
with kimshuka, muni-flowers, gokarna, nagakarna, sandhya flowers, bilvataka, ranjani, ketaki-born,
kushmanda, timira-born, those from kusha, kasha and reed, dyuta and the rest, maruvaka, and other fragrant leaves —
enjoyment, liberation and loss of sin; he is pleased by all with devotion. A flower is more than a lakh of gold; a garland a crore-fold more;
in one's own grove or another's grove, with forest-grown flowers the fruit is threefold. One should not worship Vishnu with scattered, over-limbed or crushed flowers;
with kanchanara, likewise unmatta, girikarnika, kutaja, shalmali and shirisha — hell and the like.
With fragrant Brahma-lotuses and with blue-lotus flowers, Hari; with arka, mandara and dhattura flowers Hara is worshipped;
one should not give kutaja, karkati flowers or ketaki to Shiva; what is born of kushmanda or neem is demonic and fragrance-less.
Non-violence, victory over the senses, forbearance, knowledge, compassion, learning — having worshipped the gods with flowers of feeling one gains enjoyment and liberation.
Non-violence is the first flower; restraint of the senses a flower; compassion for beings the flower of all; peace is the most distinguished flower;
calm a flower, austerity a flower, meditation the seventh flower, and truth the eighth flower; with these Keshava is pleased.
Hari worshipped with just these eight flowers is pleased. There are other, external flowers here, best of men;
Vishnu worshipped with devotion and compassion is satisfied. Water is the Varuna flower; ghee, milk and curd the Soma;
food and the like is Prajapati's; incense and lamp are Agni's; fruits, flowers and the like the Vanaspatya, fifth;
the root of kusha and the like is earthly; scent and sandal is Vayu's; the flower called faith of Vishnu; always the eight flowers;
seat, the five-limbed image, or Vishnu, the eight flowers; for Vishnu with Vasudeva and the rest, or for Shiva with Ishana and the rest.
for many kalpas pierced by spears and the like by Yama's servants; in Mahatamisra tormented by snakes, leeches and the like;
as long as the earth, matricides and the like with swords in the Asipatravana; for many kalpas in hell and in Karambha-sands;
he who burned people is burned there by sands and the like; in Kakola, the one who eats alone sweet food eats worms and filth;
in Kuttala, the one who abandons the five sacrifices eats urine and blood; in Sudurgandha, an eater of the forbidden eats blood;
in Tailapaka the tormentor of others is pressed like sesame; in Tailapaka he is cooked who kills one who sought refuge;
in Niruchchhvasa the destroyer of gifts; the seller of juices at sacrifice; named Vajrakavata; in Mahapata the liar there;
in Mahajvala the evil-minded; in Krakacha those who go to the forbidden; the mixer of castes in Gudapaka; one who pierces others' vital spots is pierced;
in Kshara-hrada the killer of beings; in Kshuradhara the land-stealer; in Ambarisha the thief of cows and gold; in Drumachchhidvajrashastraka the tree-cutter;
the honey-thief in Paritapa; in Kalasutra the thief of another's wealth; in Kashmala the great meat-eater; in Ugragandha the giver of no pinda;
in Durdhara the eater of glass and those devoted to taking prisoners; in the hell Manjusha, Loha, Apratishtha the slanderer of the Veda;
in Putivaktra the false witness; in Parilunthana the wealth-seizer; the killer of children, women and old in Karala; the tormentor of Brahmins;
in Vilepa the Brahmin drinker of liquor; in Mahatamra the fat-eater.
Likewise one who assaulted others' wives embraces a blazing iron slab; in Shalmala a woman who went to many men embraces it;
tongue-tearing, eye-piercing for looking at women; those who went to mother, daughter and the like are cast into heaps of embers;
thieves are split by razors, the meat-eater eats his own flesh; a man who does a month's fast does not go to hell;
the doer of the Ekadashi vow, the one keeping the Bhishma-panchaka.
One should avoid idle talk, give up desire for wealth; not touch anyone not keeping the vow, nor disturb those engaged in wrong acts;
one should stay in the temple of a god for thirty days. Having worshipped on the twelfth and fed the twice-born, the vower
having completed and given the fee, should break the fast; he obtains enjoyment and liberation and thirteen kalpas.
One should have a Vaishnava sacrifice performed, worship thirteen Brahmins; as many pairs of garments, vessels and seats,
umbrellas with purifiers and pairs of sandals, yoga-bands and sacred threads one should give to a Brahmin, so held;
having worshipped a golden Vishnu on a bed for another Brahmin, one should also worship one's own image with garments and the rest:
By Vishnu's grace the Brahmin is freed from all sins; I shall go to Vishnu's world; I myself become Vishnu.
Go, go, divine-minded, to Vishnu's blameless abode; there stainless in an aerial car one should stay bearing Vishnu's form.
Having told the twice-born, one should offer that bed to the teacher; having lifted a hundred families the vower leads them to Vishnu's world.
The country where a month-long faster lives becomes spotless; what then of the whole family in which there is a month-long faster?
Having seen a vower fainted, one should give milk and ghee; these do not break the vow, the oblation approved by Brahmins;
milk, the teacher's beneficial herbs, water, roots and fruits — Vishnu is the great medicine, the doer; therefore one should rescue the vow.

Son of Mitra and Varuna, pot-born, homage to you; by whom Atapi and the great demon Vatapi were eaten,
agnipuran:206:7	by whom the ocean was drunk dry — may that Agastya be before me. I shall pray to Agastya by deed, mind and speech;
agnipuran:206:8	I shall worship Maitra with desire for the other world, born in another island, dearest to the gods.
agnipuran:206:9	King of all trees, sandal, be accepted; vessel of dharma, wealth, desire and liberation, destroyer of sin.
